It fills the template: "Replace every placeholder with concrete text". `specify init` writes the template itself to that path, "if the file is missing, init creates it from the current constitution template" (https://github.com/github/spec-kit/blob/main/docs/upgrade.md), so a file that still has the template's heading, "# [PROJECT_NAME] Constitution" (https://github.com/github/spec-kit/blob/main/templates/constitution-template.md), is the template and no planning document, as in appsflyersdk/appsflyer-react-native-plugin and containers/fetchit. The row reads the opening, so a constitution that is a link, which the copy stores as its marker, does not count.

Spec Kit 0.0.1 to 0.0.21 put its files at the project root, among them the constitution and its update checklist: "When amending the constitution (`/memory/constitution.md`), ensure all dependent documents are updated to maintain consistency." (https://github.com/github/spec-kit/blob/v0.0.21/memory/constitution_update_checklist.md), and the plan command read it: "Read the constitution at `/memory/constitution.md` to understand constitutional requirements." (https://github.com/github/spec-kit/blob/v0.0.21/templates/commands/plan.md). The live page still names it: "The constitution (`memory/constitution.md`) acts as the architectural DNA of the system". Version 0.0.22 moved the files into .specify/: "docs: fix the paths of generated files (moved under a `.specify/` folder)" (https://github.com/github/spec-kit/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md). memory/constitution.md is a common name, so the row reads it beside the update checklist that those versions put into the same folder, and leaves out the template that they put there unfilled, "# [PROJECT_NAME] Constitution" (https://github.com/github/spec-kit/blob/v0.0.21/memory/constitution.md). No repository of the October collection has the layout.

smart-ralph's ralph-speckit is a "Spec-driven development plugin for Claude Code using the [GitHub spec-kit](https://github.com/github/spec-kit) methodology." Its directory structure has ".specify/" with "001-feature-name/" below "specs/", and "| `spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md` | Feature specifications | committed |", while ".speckit-state.json" and ".progress.md" are ignored. Spec Kit itself writes no .specify/specs/, and this row comes before Spec Kit's rows, which would read the folder beside .specify/. No repository of the October collection has the layout.

The folder counts beside a .specify/ at its project root or above, because specs/<NNN>-<slug>/ alone is a common layout. The feature folder's "default location is under `specs/` in that project" (https://github.com/github/spec-kit/blob/main/docs/overview/core.md).

The writing-plans skill: "**Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`" and "(User preferences for plan location override this default)". A person's preference can therefore send the plans into .claude/plans/, the folder of the plans of Claude Code's plan mode, and this row comes before the row of claude. A file there counts when its opening names the plan's executor as the template writes it: "> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development". jirkapok/GasPlanner's .claude/CLAUDE.md tells the skill to "write the implementation plan into `.claude/plans/` (not the skill's default `docs/superpowers/plans/`)", and its plan there opens with that header (planning_precision pd-0090 of the evaluation of 2026-11-04), as readest/readest's plans in apps/readest-app/.claude/plans/ do.

Claude Code's plan mode writes each plan as a Markdown file into the folder that plansDirectory names: "Choose where Claude Code stores the plan files it writes in plan mode. Claude Code resolves the path relative to the project root." The setting has "Scope: Any file" and "Default: unset, so Claude Code uses `~/.claude/plans`". Any settings file can set it, including a person's ~/.claude/settings.json and the gitignored .claude/settings.local.json, so a repository can hold the plans in .claude/plans/ without a setting that it commits, as the evidence shows. Plan mode writes the files into the folder itself and names them after the prompt: "Plan files are now named after your prompt (e.g. `fix-auth-race-snug-otter.md`) instead of purely random words" (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md, version 2.1.111). Of the files in .claude/plans/ in the October collection, only promregator/promregator's this-project-currently-istwinkly-thimble.md has a name of that form, and the others, such as forcedotcom/salesforcedx-vscode's W-22888206.md, have names that people gave them, so the row counts the plans that a repository keeps in that folder, not only the plans that plan mode wrote. A file in a folder below it, such as harness/canary's .claude/plans/result/02-25-26.md, or in another format, such as chrisbenincasa/tunarr's .claude/plans/defect-register.html, stays an unclassified file. A plan of superpowers there is counted by the row of superpowers before this one.

Cursor's Plan Mode saves a plan to the workspace on request: "Tip: Click "Save to workspace" to store plans in .cursor/plans/ ." Cursor's staff on the forum: "you can move a plan into a project using Save to Workspace." (https://forum.cursor.com/t/option-to-save-plans-in-project-level-cursor-directory/152291). The documentation (https://cursor.com/docs/agent/plan-mode) names no file name or format. The files that Cursor writes open with a front matter with name and overview and end in .plan.md, or, in older versions, open with a comment of two UUIDs, with or without that suffix, as forcedotcom/salesforcedx-vscode's simplify-packaging-org-ext.md shows (evidence). .cursor/plans/ also holds files that people write, which the opening leaves out.

Gemini CLI's Plan Mode writes its plans outside the project unless a setting names a folder, since by default they "are stored in a managed temporary directory outside your project". The page gives .gemini/plans as the example of that folder: "For example, to store plans in a `.gemini/plans` directory within your project:". A person's own settings can name it, so the folder counts without a committed setting.

The agents page states "With OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_PLAN_MODE enabled, Plan saves its plan to .opencode/plans/ for Git projects, or to the plans/ directory under OpenCode's data directory otherwise." OpenCode 1.19.3 of 2026-10-16 names the file <created>-<slug>.md there, and in its data directory outside a git repository (plan in https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/e3c4eb242585dcd77be1a867391b7c25fd47ce52/packages/opencode/src/session/session.ts), and lets its plan agent edit any Markdown file of the folder. A completed epic moves whole (https://github.com/automazeio/ccpm/blob/main/skill/ccpm/references/sync.md): "mv .claude/epics/<name> .claude/epics/archived/", and version 1 moved it to .claude/epics/.archived/ (https://github.com/automazeio/ccpm/blob/abfd4ff740dd4505aebd873be2d935553ed29f50/ccpm/commands/pm/epic-close.md): "Move epic directory to .claude/epics/.archived/{epic_name}/".

Version 1 of ccpm is kept on the v1 branch, whose README points to the current version that works "with any Agent Skills–compatible harness (Factory, Claude Code, Amp, Cursor, OpenCode, and more)". Version 1 wrote the project context into .claude/context/: "context/ # Project-wide context files", and "agents read from .claude/context/". Its /context:create command (https://github.com/automazeio/ccpm/blob/abfd4ff740dd4505aebd873be2d935553ed29f50/ccpm/commands/context/create.md) writes nine files: "progress.md ... project-structure.md ... tech-context.md ... system-patterns.md ... product-context.md ... project-brief.md ... project-overview.md ... project-vision.md ... project-style-guide.md". .claude/context/ is also a common folder of a project's own, so a file counts beside ccpm's .claude/prds/, .claude/epics/ or .claude/commands/pm/ alone: "pm/ # ← Project management commands (this system)" and "prds/ # ← PM's PRD files".
